veridian.context:
Matter: In re Veridian Orthopedics ApexHip Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 3102 (N.D. Ind.).
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. (Warsaw, Indiana) manufactures the ApexHip metal-on-metal total hip system,
cleared by FDA in March 2017 and withdrawn from the market in February 2024. Plaintiffs allege that
ApexHip sheds cobalt and chromium wear debris causing tissue damage and early revision surgery, that
Veridian failed to warn, promoted the device to younger and more active patients, and paid consulting
surgeons to promote it. A separate June 2022 recall of acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299
concerned coating adhesion. Veridian also sells KneeFlex knee implants, the legacy ClassicHip, and
ShoulderPro; those products are not at issue. The relevant period is January 1, 2015 through June 30, 2024.
Custodians are current and former Veridian employees. "Document" includes emails, chats, texts,
memoranda, reports, minutes, presentations, spreadsheets, forms, and letters.

metal ion testing, fatigue testing, and any test protocols, reports, or raw data, whether performed by
Veridian or by any third-party laboratory; (e) design changes, engineering change orders, or proposed
design changes, whether or not implemented; and (f) the design history file and any index thereto.
"ApexHip system" includes the femoral stem, femoral head, acetabular cup, and KinetiCoat coating.

documents.text:
From: Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
To: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2019 16:42
Subject: RE: Sales talking points and the deferred ECO

Tom—

Understood. I’m not looking to relitigate the ECO decision in a sales deck, and I’ll keep the deck focused on cleared indications and the existing evidence package.

I do need a clean answer for the field language. The current durability slide says “engineered for sustained performance in active patients” and the speaker notes reference the large-head stability story. Is there anything we should take out or qualify now that ECO-2019-118 is deferred? Off the record, I’m trying to avoid creating a situation where a rep is making a statement we would not stand behind later.

If you can send the specific wording you would be comfortable with, I can route it through Quality/RA with the regular deck refresh. We have the regional managers asking for the July version by Friday.

Carlos

-----Original Message-----
From: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>
To: Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2019 14:58
Subject: RE: Sales talking points and the deferred ECO

carlos —

i would not say, or imply, that the cup is validated beyond 45 degrees inclination. it isn't. the protocol we ran for the original design verification was 45 degrees under ISO 14242. the follow-up work at 55 showed materially higher wear with edge loading. that's what i laid out in the february memo to you, priya, and dana.

the ECO being deferred does not make that result disappear. if the durability language can be read as “works the same at any surgical angle” then yes, it needs to be corrected in the materials. reps should stay with the cleared labeling and not freelance on cup position, longevity, or wear at high inclination.

i know that is not a great sales answer, but it is the accurate one.

tom

-----Original Message-----
From: Carlos Mendes <cmendes@veridianortho.com>
To: Tom Halvorsen <thalvorsen@veridianortho.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2019 13:21
Subject: Sales talking points and the deferred ECO

Tom,

Quick question as I update the Apex sales deck for the summer regional meetings.

With ECO-2019-118 deferred, do we need to alter any of the durability language or the “active adult” messaging? The field is still using the standard longevity/stability slides, and I don’t want to overcorrect based on an internal engineering discussion if the product positioning has not changed.

Can you give me your view before I circulate a draft?

Thanks,
Carlos

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Financial Planning & Analysis
Recall Cost Estimate Summary

To: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer; Rachel Steinberg, General Counsel
From: Hannah Berg, FP&A Manager
Date: June 20, 2022
Subject: Apex Recall Cost Estimate - Cup Lots V-2200-V-2299

Attached is the current working estimate for direct costs associated with the June 14 voluntary Class II recall of ApexHip cup lots V-2200 through V-2299. This is based on the distribution file provided by Quality as of Friday afternoon: 1,140 units distributed, of which 412 are currently identified as implanted.

The estimate assumes replacement availability from unaffected inventory, return freight paid by Veridian, and reimbursement of reasonable hospital labor/handling charges for product quarantine, return processing, and replacement cases where applicable. We have included a customer goodwill credit pool for accounts with significant disruption; this has not yet been allocated by account.

| Cost Category | Basis / Assumption | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---:|
| Replacement inventory | 1,140 distributed units; transfer-cost basis for replacement cups and associated field kit utilization | $1,185,000 |
| Shipping and return logistics | Outbound replacement shipments, prepaid returns, expedited shipments for implanted-patient cases | $465,000 |
| Hospital handling fees | Quarantine, inventory reconciliation, return processing, and documented replacement-case support for 412 implanted units | $1,230,000 |
| Customer goodwill credits | Estimated credits for affected hospital accounts and distributor adjustments | $520,000 |
| Recall administration / communications | Customer notices, call-center support, effectiveness checks, and outside logistics support | $215,000 |
| Total estimated direct recall cost |  | $3,615,000 |

For planning purposes, I would carry approximately $3.4M-$3.6M pending completion of account-level reconciliation and final hospital submissions. The largest variable remains hospital handling and replacement-case reimbursement, particularly where facilities request charges beyond product handling.

This estimate is limited to the coating-related cup recall and should not be combined with the separate metal-ion/ARMD litigation exposure. Any potential claims reserve related to elevated cobalt/chromium levels, revision allegations, or other Apex product-liability matters is being tracked separately with Legal and Risk Management.

I will refresh the file once Quality completes its first effectiveness-check cycle and Sales confirms the goodwill-credit recommendations.

All documents constituting, reflecting, or relating to the design and development of the ApexHip system,
including without limitation: (a) design inputs, user needs, and design requirements; (b) risk analyses,
including any FMEA, hazard analysis, or risk management file; (c) design reviews and design review
meeting materials; (d) verification and validation testing, including wear testing, tribology testing,
metal ion testing, fatigue testing, and any test protocols, reports, or raw data, whether performed by
Veridian or by any third-party laboratory; (e) design changes, engineering change orders, or proposed
design changes, whether or not implemented; and (f) the design history file and any index thereto.
"ApexHip system" includes the femoral stem, femoral head, acetabular cup, and KinetiCoat coating.

criteria.true:
The document concerns the design, development, testing, or modification of the ApexHip system: design
inputs and requirements, FMEA or risk analysis, design reviews, verification and validation testing
(wear, tribology, metal ion, fatigue) by Veridian or a lab, engineering change orders or proposed design
changes, or the design history file.
criteria.false:
The document does not concern ApexHip design, testing, or design changes. Design documents for other
products, and ApexHip documents about sales, marketing, complaints (without engineering analysis),
regulatory filings that do not discuss design, or finances, are not responsive.

__gate__.instructions:
Does this document substantively concern the ApexHip hip implant (its design, testing, manufacturing,
recall, complaints, regulatory status, marketing, sales, surgeon relationships, registry data, or
finances), or is it a personnel record for someone on the ApexHip, Quality, or Regulatory Affairs teams?
Answer no for documents about other products, general company business, IT, facilities, or social matters
that only mention ApexHip in passing or not at all.

request.aggregate: p = noul; then p = p × p(gate); label = responsive if p ≥ 0.5

mnk.context:
Matter: opioid litigation against Mallinckrodt plc and Mallinckrodt LLC (MDL 2804, In re National Prescription
Opiate Litigation, and related state actions). Mallinckrodt was among the largest U.S. manufacturers of generic
opioids (oxycodone, hydrocodone, methadone) and also sold branded opioids including Exalgo (hydromorphone ER),
Roxicodone, and Methadose. Plaintiffs allege that Mallinckrodt failed to maintain effective controls against
diversion, including its suspicious order monitoring (SOM) program for wholesaler and distributor orders; that it
had, through chargeback and IMS data, visibility into downstream distribution to pharmacies (including Florida
"pill mills") and did not act on it; that it promoted opioids while minimizing addiction risk; and that it sought
ever-larger DEA production quota. Mallinckrodt also sold non-opioid products (e.g. Ofirmev, INOmax, Acthar,
contrast agents) that are not at issue. The relevant period is 2006 through 2017. The documents are emails,
reproduced with their headers as a reviewer would see them; quoted earlier messages in a thread are part of the
document. Newsletters and mass mailings received by an employee are documents in that employee's files.

From: Harper, Karen
Sent: Wednesday, August 12, 2009 7:28 AM
To: Pokorny, Camille M
Cc: Ratliff, Bill; Stewart, Cathy; Hunter, Dave
Subject: Southern California Compounding Pharmacy Order Inquiry
Camille,
Per our conversations, customer has inquired about increasing the frequency of their Fentanyl orders or increasing the quantity of
their Fentanyl orders.
Further, they intend to purchase Hydromorphone powder as well.
Customer operates using a Retail Pharmacy DEA Registration.

Mallinckrodt interpretation of the regulations is as follows:

Retail Pharmacy
Compounds medications to fit the unique needs of the patient, as authorized by a prescription from physician.
The medications must be dispensed directly to a patient and not sent to the physician.
DEA does not  require  quota issuance for acquisitions by Retail Pharmacy registrants, distributions of CI and CII require DEA
222 order forms.
Note: The Mallinckrodt business model does not include direct sales to Retail Pharmacy registrants.

Compounding Pharmacy
Compounds medications to fit the unique needs of the patient, as authorized by a prescription from physician.
Compounding pharmacy does not dispense medication to the patient but may send it directly to the prescribing physician for
office administration.
DEA requires Compounding Pharmacy registrants to be licensed within the category of Manufacturing registrants.
Manufacturing registrants require quota  for acquisitions of CI and CII controlled substances, distributions of CI and CII require
DEA 222 order forms.
Note: The Mallinckrodt business model accommodates sales to Compounding Pharmacy/Manufacturing registrants, upon proof
of current DEA registration license, provided they certify in writing that the firm has available Procurement Quota issued by DEA,
adequate to cover the quantity of the specific sale.

Hi Sanjeev,

Hope your week has been going well. I've updated the 795 Market potential bubble chart you saw a couple weeks ago. Sorry for the delay in sending this to you, but I thought it would be better  to wait for the new target list that was recently drafted for a different project. The top chart is the new chart with our target list only. The bottom is with all physicians. Relatively speaking, there are many similarities.  The biggest takeaways to me are the changes for the Orthopedics, General Practice, and ER specialties. Orthopedics are now the specialty with the highest total value, however they are still the least likely to write low dose Rxs and are also less likely to use Oxy Combos compared to Oxy ER/Oxy IR.  General Practice is still a top player, but without the low volume writers removed in the targeting calculations, they begin to look similar to ER physicians and Orthopedics in terms of overall volume. ER physicians have also shifted upwards and while not quite the value of General Practice as a whole, they are slightly more likely to write lower dose Rxs and use Oxy Combos in those low dose Rxs. cuad.context:
Matter: legal due diligence in connection with a corporate transaction. Counsel is reviewing the target
company's commercial contracts (license, distribution, supply, services, marketing, joint venture, and
similar agreements) to locate provisions that bear on the deal. The documents are excerpts from those
contracts: one paragraph or clause at a time, shown with the contract's title and its position in the
agreement. An excerpt is responsive to a request if the excerpt itself contains the kind of provision
the request describes (in whole or in substantial part). Excerpts that merely define a term, reference a
section elsewhere, or discuss a neighbouring topic are not responsive. Each excerpt is judged on its own.

request.rule: score saturates with the number of distinct terms present (~3 hits → 0.5, ~8 → 0.9); label = responsive if score ≥ 0.5
score saturates with the number of distinct terms present (~3 hits → 0.5, ~8 → 0.9); label = responsive if score ≥ 0.5

workflow: Control set: the reviewer codes a simple random sample of the collection first (10% of the pool, capped at 500 and sized for at least ~30 relevant documents; a fixed 2,000 on TREC's 286k collection). These documents never enter the review queue and are not trained on; their coding counts as review effort and their codes are part of the production set.
Seed: random documents plus the same number of the strongest keyword-floor hits, coded by the reviewer (50 + 50 on the 800-document Mallinckrodt pool, 100 + 100 elsewhere).
Fit TF-IDF + balanced logistic regression on everything queued and coded so far for any-issue relevance.
Rank the collection; the reviewer codes the top uncoded batch (50 / 100 / 1,000 documents by collection size), tagging issues as they go.

workflow: Draw a random sample of N documents from the collection.
A reviewer reads each and codes it for every issue (simulated here from the gold labels; 50 documents/hour, $65/hour).
Fit TF-IDF (word 1-2 grams, sublinear tf) and balanced logistic regression: one model for any-issue relevance and one per issue with at least 5 coded positives.
Choose each model's cutoff by 5-fold cross-validation on the coded sample only: the score that keeps 80% of the sample's positives (or, in the F1 variant, the score that maximises F1).
Score the rest of the collection. A document is produced on an issue when it clears the relevance cutoff and that issue's cutoff; the coded documents keep the reviewer's codes.

trec.context:
Matter: a public-records request against the Executive Office of the Governor of Florida, covering email sent
or received by Governor Jeb Bush and his staff during his two terms (1999-2007). The collection is government
email: constituent letters, staff correspondence, press clippings and news forwards, scheduling, legislation
and budget traffic, agency reports, and personal messages. Emails are shown with their headers, as a reviewer
would see them; quoted earlier messages and forwarded articles are part of the document.

Each request names an issue. The requesting party reads every request at the level of the issue, not the
sentence: an email is responsive if it substantively concerns the issue, its background, the policy fights and
legislation around it, or its consequences in Florida, even when the request's exact words never appear. A
constituent asking the Governor to sign or veto a bill on the issue is responsive. A passing use of a word
from the request, with no substantive connection to the issue, is not. Note that "Governor Bush" and "Jeb" in
these emails refer to Jeb Bush, the Governor of Florida, not to his brother the President.

workflow: Control set: the reviewer codes a simple random sample of the collection first (10% of the pool, capped at 500 and sized for at least ~30 relevant documents; a fixed 2,000 on TREC's 286k collection). These documents never enter the review queue and are not trained on; their coding counts as review effort and their codes are part of the production set.
Seed: random documents plus the same number of the strongest keyword-floor hits, coded by the reviewer (50 + 50 on the 800-document Mallinckrodt pool, 100 + 100 elsewhere).
Fit TF-IDF + balanced logistic regression on everything queued and coded so far for any-issue relevance.
Rank the collection; the reviewer codes the top uncoded batch (50 / 100 / 1,000 documents by collection size), tagging issues as they go.

Estimate recall from the control set: whenever a batch is picked, every control document scoring at or above the batch's lowest queued score counts as reached from then on (it would have been in the batch had it not been held out); recall is the share of control-set documents coded relevant that have been reached. Repeat 3-5 and stop once the estimate is at or above the target (80%; 75% in the 'cal_75' variant) for two consecutive batches, or when the pool is exhausted. (The 'knee stop' variant uses Cormack & Grossman's knee method and no control set.)

The production set is everything the reviewer coded relevant, control set included; that is what the site plots, scored against gold on the pool CAL ran over. The review set (everything read), the recall estimate at stop against the true figure, and the classifier applied on its own to the evaluation set at the control-set cutoff are reported alongside.

workflow: Draw a random sample of N documents from the collection.
A reviewer reads each and codes it for every issue (simulated here from the gold labels; 50 documents/hour, $65/hour).
Fit TF-IDF (word 1-2 grams, sublinear tf) and balanced logistic regression: one model for any-issue relevance and one per issue with at least 5 coded positives.
Choose each model's cutoff by 5-fold cross-validation on the coded sample only: the score that keeps 80% of the sample's positives (or, in the F1 variant, the score that maximises F1).
Score the rest of the collection. A document is produced on an issue when it clears the relevance cutoff and that issue's cutoff; the coded documents keep the reviewer's codes.

jev.base: The default. One Noul question per issue: a yes/no question whose answer is a probability. The RFP text is the instruction; the positive and negative descriptions from the task file are the true/false criteria. The state is a structured object with the matter background and the document.
jev.choice: Same instruction and criteria, but asked as a Choice between the two labels rather than a yes/no Noul. The model returns a probability for each label and picks one; p(responsive) is what we score.
jev.score: Asked as a Score on a five-point ordinal scale from 'clearly not responsive' to 'clearly responsive'. The criteria are folded into the instruction text. The scored probability is the level divided by four.
jev.crit_none: The Noul question with no criteria at all: only the instruction. Tests how much the true/false descriptions are doing.
jev.crit_struct: Criteria supplied as the structured object from the task file (what / includes / excludes / examples) instead of prose. Falls back to prose where a question has no structured block.
jev.literal: Instruction replaced by the plain-language 'literal' phrasing from the task file (a reviewer's one-line version) instead of the verbatim RFP text.
jev.no_context: The matter background is dropped from the state; the model sees only the document.
jev.state_string: The state is a single flat string ('MATTER BACKGROUND: ... DOCUMENT: ...') instead of a structured object with named fields. This lever won the Veridian dev split and is the recipe.
jev.gate: An extra Noul asks whether the document has anything to do with the matter at all. Each issue probability is multiplied by the gate probability.
jev.ensemble: Three phrasings of the same question (RFP text, literal, title + positive description) are asked as three Nouls and their probabilities averaged.
jev.decompose: Where the task file breaks an issue into atomic sub-questions, each is asked as its own Noul and the issue probability is the max across them (logical OR).
jev.preview: Identical request to the default, sent to the jev-preview model instead of jev-1.13.0.

laya.base: Same request shape as Jev's default, run through the local Laya encoder. Laya packs the question head into at most 192 tokens and the whole input into 512, so on these corpora the RFP instruction and criteria are silently truncated and most documents are cut from the right.
laya.choice: Choice over the two labels instead of Noul.
laya.score: Five-level Score with the criteria folded into the instruction.
laya.literal: Instruction replaced by the shorter literal phrasing; fits more of the question into the 192-token head.
laya.gate: An extra matter-relevance Noul gates each issue probability.
laya.ensemble: Three phrasings averaged; each is truncated the same way.
laya.compact: A one-line instruction ('Is this document responsive to the request for production about: <title>?') and one-sentence criteria, sized to fit Laya's 192-token head so nothing in the question is truncated.
laya.chunk: The document is split into overlapping windows sized to Laya's remaining context (about 300 tokens), each window is scored, and the per-question probability is the max over windows. Up to 16 windows.
laya.recipe: compact + chunk: the two levers that address Laya's 512-token context. Neither changes what is being asked; both change how much of it Laya can actually read.
laya.recipe_choice: compact + chunk with the Choice form.

notes.llm: One chat completion with a system prompt, a user message (matter background, the request block with responsive / not-responsive criteria, the document), and a JSON schema the vendor enforces on the output. The model returns a label and p_responsive; there is no free text. The prefix (everything before the document) is identical across documents so prompt caches can hit.

score_levels: Clearly not responsive to the request
Borderline; a reviewer could go either way
